subject: Genetics
title: Cancer Genomics
description: A short lesson to help you apply Cancer Genomics.

hook.text: Every cancer has a unique set of mutations. Sequencing tumors reveals which drugs will work—and which won't.

buildup.text: The Cancer Genome Atlas sequenced 33 cancer types. It found cancers from different organs sometimes share mutations.

discovery.text: Targeted therapies attack specific mutations. Imatinib cured a once-fatal leukemia by blocking one mutant protein.

twist.text: Tumors evolve resistance. Like bacteria versus antibiotics, cancer cells mutate to dodge treatment.

climax.text: Liquid biopsies now detect cancer DNA in blood. Tumors leave traces that sequencing can catch before symptoms appear.

punchline.text: Sequencing doesn't just find cancer. It finds its weakness.

quiz.question: What does a liquid biopsy detect?
